MOD_VOY_RULE_NOUN_Mining: Mountain or Highlands, or a mine
MOD_VOY_RULE_NOUN_Crafting: a workshop, town, camp or port
MOD_VOY_RULE_NOUN_Runecrafting: a magic site, temple or the capital
MOD_VOY_RULE_NOUN_Summoning: a monolith, magic site or temple
MOD_VOY_NOTICE_NO_AOD: Voyage: Far Shores needs Atlas of Discovery and stays dormant.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_COMPASS_DESC: Warms when you walk toward the nearest place where a locked skill works, and points the way. It never names the place.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_PITCH_DESC: Pine tar boiled down by the fire. With logs, it repairs a ship's hull on the Voyage page. Firemaking makes it now and then.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_PROSPECTORS_NOTES_DESC: A prospector's notes on where one ore runs. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Mining rock.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_FORESTERS_SURVEY_DESC: A forester's survey of where one tree grows. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Woodcutting tree.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_ANGLERS_LOG_DESC: An angler's log of where one fish bites. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Fishing spot.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_FARMERS_ALMANAC_DESC: A farmer's almanac of where one crop takes. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Farming seed.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_FENCES_LEDGER_DESC: A fence's ledger of where one mark can be found. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Thieving target.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_STAR_CHART_DESC: A star chart of where one constellation stands clear. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Astrology constellation.
MOD_VOY_MILESTONE_1: Compass: how close and which way
MOD_VOY_MILESTONE_3: Compass: the name of the place
MOD_VOY_SETTING_STRICTNESS_HINT_STRICT: Strict: gathering needs terrain, crafting needs a workshop or town.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_STRICTNESS_HINT_RELAXED: Relaxed: only gathering is tied to terrain.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_OVERLAY_HINT: Tint surveyed hexes by terrain on the Cartography map.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_RULES_HINT: Off: nothing is locked by location; the overlay and the panel stay.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_ZONES_HINT: Each ore, tree, fish, crop, thieving target and constellation is found only in some places: copper in dry red country, salmon in cold rivers, the northern stars in the north.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_COMBAT_HINT: Fight only where the combat area is on the map, or right next to it. Dungeons and strongholds too.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_TRADE_HINT: Sell and buy only in or next to a town, port or market.
MOD_VOY_NOTICE_TABLE_MISMATCH: Voyage: the map differs from the terrain table. Location rules are off until the mod is updated.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLURB_DINGHY: A small rowing boat. It stays within 2 hexes of land and you can board or leave it on any coast.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_BLOCK_RULES_OFF: Voyage rules are off: turn them on in the mod settings (Location rules) to build a ship.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_BLOCK_NOT_COAST: Stand on a coast hex, next to water you have surveyed, to launch it.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_BLOCK_NO_MATERIALS: Not enough GP or logs: the cost is above, with what you have in brackets.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_BUILT: Your dinghy is in the water. Step onto it to board.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_AT_SEA: You are out on the water, so the boat under you is now your dinghy.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_OVERSEAS: The boat you hired to get here is yours now: your dinghy is moored on the nearest coast of this land.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_NEED_BOAT_WATER: You need a ship to go on the water. Build a dinghy on the Voyage page.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_NEED_BOAT_LAND: No way there on foot. You need a ship: build a dinghy on the Voyage page.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_ISLAND_LOCKED: Your ${hull} can't land on ${island}: it needs a ${needed}.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_TOO_FAR: Too far out for your ${hull}: it keeps within ${reach} hexes of a coast it can land on.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_MOORED: No way there on foot. Your ${hull} is moored ${where}; walk to it to sail.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_OTHER_WATER: Your ${hull} can't get there: this water doesn't connect to the sea it is on.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_OUT_OF_REACH: Your ${hull} can't get there: it keeps within ${reach} hexes of land.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_NO_SHIP: The ship isn't available: the Voyage skill didn't load. Check the console for a [Voyage] error.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_NO_SHIP_YET: No ship yet. You travel on foot.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_BUILD_HINT: It goes into the water next to you.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_RULES_OFF: Voyage rules are off: you can walk on the water, and your ship follows when you step onto the sea. Turn them on in the mod settings.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_FUTURE_SAVE: This save comes from a newer Voyage build: progress is kept but not counted here.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_COMPASS_STAGE_1: How close (Hot, Warm, Cold, Freezing) and which way
MOD_VOY_PAGE_COMPASS_STAGE_3: Also the name of the place
MOD_VOY_PAGE_COMPASS_MISSING: The compass is not in your bank. The shop sells another under Voyage.
MOD_VOY_GATE_NEAREST_GRACE: Nearest place it works: ${where}, next to ${match}.
MOD_VOY_GATE_NONE_KNOWN: You know of no ${need} yet. Survey the hexes around you in Cartography to find one.
MOD_VOY_GATE_AREA_STAND: You must stand on ${name} or next to it to fight there.
MOD_VOY_GATE_AREA_HERE: From here you can fight in ${names}.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_NEEDS: ${name} is not found here. Look around ${need}.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_NONE_KNOWN: No place for it is known yet: survey more of the map.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_STOPPED: ${name} stopped: it is not found here.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_SKY_NEEDS: ${name} cannot be seen from here. It shows ${where}.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_SKY_DARK: Stars need a dark, open sky: not next to a town, not under a forest.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_LAT_NORTH: in the north, at row ${row} or further north
MOD_VOY_ZONE_LAT_SOUTH: in the south, at row ${row} or further south
MOD_VOY_GATE_AREA_UNKNOWN: You do not know where ${name} is yet. Survey the hexes around you in Cartography to find it.
MOD_VOY_GATE_TRADE_ONLY_SELL: You can sell only in a town, port or market, or next to one.
MOD_VOY_GATE_TRADE_ONLY_BUY: You can buy only in a town, port or market, or next to one.
MOD_VOY_GATE_TRADE_NONE_KNOWN: You know of no trading place yet. Survey the hexes around you in Cartography to find one.
MOD_VOY_GATE_TRADE_TITLE: No one to trade with here
MOD_VOY_GATE_STOPPED: ${name} stopped: it does not work here.
MOD_VOY_GATE_FIGHT_LEFT: You left ${name}: the fight is over.
MOD_VOY_GATE_FIGHT_OUT_OF_REACH: ${name} is out of reach from here: the fight is over.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_ZONE_NONE: Nothing for your level is found here.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_SKY_NONE: ${skill}: none of your constellations can be seen here.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_STRANDED_HINT: You cannot afford the road to a place where you can earn GP.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_TRADER_HERE_HINT: Selling works here at half price until you can afford the road to a trading place.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_TRADER_HERE: A wandering trader is here (half price)
MOD_VOY_PANEL_NO_TRADE_HINT: Sell, buy and trade only in a town, port or market, or next to one.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_COMBAT_HINT: Combat areas you can enter from this hex: you stand on the area or right next to it. Click a name to open it.
MOD_VOY_MINI_LOAD_HINT: You can load stores here: open the Voyage page
MOD_VOY_MINI_PLAN_HINT: Planned voyage: ${name}, ${hexes} away. Open the plan
MOD_VOY_PANEL_TABLE_MISMATCH: Map differs from the terrain table: rules off.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_LEFT_BEHIND: You leave the wandering trader behind.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_MOVES_ON: The wandering trader moves on: you can afford the road now.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_ARRIVES: Looks like you're stranded here. Good timing: a wandering trader is just passing by.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_HALF_PRICE: He looks over your goods and offers half of what a market would pay. You see his eyes spark for a moment: he knows you have no other choice.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_STAYS: He stays until you can afford the road to a trading place.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_SPARES_COMBAT: You have nothing worth selling. He sighs and spares you ${gp} GP, just enough for the road to ${area}: the hex at (${at}), ${hexes} ${dir}. "Fight for your coin there," he says, "and sell what you find."
MOD_VOY_TRADER_SPARES_STEP: You have nothing worth selling, and nothing grows or swims here. He sighs and spares you ${gp} GP, just enough for one step ${dir}.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_NO_ROAD: You have nothing worth selling, and he has no road to point you to. He shrugs and walks on.
MOD_VOY_UNLOCK_BOTH: Voyage unlocked Cartography and the Voyage skill for you. Your next skill unlock costs two steps more.
MOD_VOY_UNLOCK_CARTOGRAPHY: Voyage unlocked Cartography for you. Your next skill unlock costs one step more.
MOD_VOY_UNLOCK_VOYAGE: Voyage unlocked the Voyage skill for you. Your next skill unlock costs one step more.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_PROVISIONS_HINT: Every hex costs food and fuel from the stores you load on the Voyage page; hard and cold ground burn more. Sailing wears the hull, which you repair with logs and Pitch. Easy ground stays walkable on empty stores.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_NIGHT_HINT: From 21:00 to 05:00 on your own clock, the fuel a trip leaves over lights the way, and every lit hex gives 25% more Voyage XP. Light never takes fuel the trip needs, so night is never worse than day. Off: it is always day.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_NIGHT_SHIFT_HINT: From -12 to 12. With 2, night runs from 23:00 to 07:00.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_CENTRE_KEY_HINT: One letter or digit, G by default. On the Cartography page it does what the map's home button does. Leave it empty to turn it off.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_JOURNAL_KEY_HINT: One letter or digit, J by default. Opens the Captain's Journal from any page and closes it again. Leave it empty to turn it off.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_FOOD: This trip needs ${need} HP of food; your stores hold ${have}. The food runs out ${hexes} along, entering ${terrain}.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_FUEL: This trip needs ${need} fuel for the campfires; your stores hold ${have}. The fuel runs out ${hexes} along, entering ${terrain}.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HOP: Sailing ${hexes} hexes to that port needs ${need} HP of food; your stores hold ${have}.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_ASHORE: This voyage needs ${trip} HP of food and would leave ${left} HP at sea, short of the ${need} HP for the way back to the coast (your stores hold ${have}).
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HINT_SEA: Sail a shorter way, or load food on the Voyage page at a port, town, market, farm, village or camp.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HINT: Load food and fuel on the Voyage page at a port, town, market, farm, village or camp. Easy ground (Grasslands, Kingslands, Beach, Desert, Swamplands) can still be walked on empty stores, for no Voyage XP.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HULL: Your ${hull}'s hull is at ${cond}%. This voyage would wear it ${need}%, and it gives out ${hexes} along.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_DEEP: Your ${hull}'s hull is at ${cond}%. Below ${worn}% it keeps out of deep water (3 or more hexes from land).
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HULL_ASHORE: This voyage would leave your ${hull}'s hull too worn to get back ashore. Keep ${need}% for the way to the coast; it is at ${cond}% now.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HULL_HINT: Repair it on the Voyage page with logs and Pitch: beach it on a coast and stand on it or next to it. A step closer to the coast always goes, however worn the hull.
MOD_VOY_STORES_RESCUE: A wandering trader knows the way out. He walks you to easier ground or a place to load, ${hexes} ${dir}: nothing from your stores and no Voyage XP for it, the road's GP as usual if you have it.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_SHORT: Not enough to go: load more at a port, town, market, farm, village or camp.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_ASHORE: Keep food to get back ashore.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_HUNGRY: ${hexes} walked hungry, for no Voyage XP.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_HULL: The hull is too worn for this.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_LIGHT: Night: ${fuel} spare fuel lights ${lit} of ${hexes} hexes (+${bonus}% Voyage XP each).
MOD_VOY_STORES_KIT: Your stores are packed for the road: ${amounts}. Load more on the Voyage page at a port, town, market, farm, village or camp.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_STORES_OFF: Provisions are off (setting or map rules): moves take nothing from the stores.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_STORES_NO_LOADING: Nothing to load here: stores load at a port, town, market, farm, village or camp.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_STORES_NOTHING: Your bank has no food or fuel this place takes: bring food, logs or Firemaking products.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_NIGHT_OFF: Night is off (setting): it is always day.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLOCK_BEACH: Beach your ${hull} first: it must be next to land, with you on it or beside it.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLOCK_MATERIALS: Needs ${logs} logs and ${pitch} Pitch for every ${step}%.
MOD_VOY_HOLD_EMPTY: Empty. Stow items from the bank: select one, and the hold is under Sell.
MOD_VOY_HOLD_AMOUNT: Type how many to stow (1 or more), or pick All.
MOD_VOY_HOLD_FULL_PAGE: The hold is full: take something out, or stow more of a kind already aboard.
MOD_VOY_HOLD_AWAY: Your ${hull} is ${where}: stand on it or next to it to use the hold.
MOD_VOY_HOLD_FULL: Your ${hull}'s hold has no free slot.
MOD_VOY_HOLD_BANK_FULL: Your bank has no free slot for it.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_STORES_LOAD_HINT: You can load here: food at ${food}%, fuel at ${fuel}%.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_NIGHT_HINT: At night the fuel a trip leaves over lights the way: ${land} a land hex, ${sea} at sea. Every lit hex gives ${bonus}% more Voyage XP; light never takes fuel the trip needs.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_HOP_NO_BOAT: Fast travel between ports is sailing: bring your ship to this port's quay first.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_HOP_AWAY: Fast travel is sailing: bring your ${hull} to this port's quay first (it is ${where}).
MOD_VOY_PANEL_HUNGRY_HINT: Your stores can't pay the way to easier ground or a place to load. A wandering trader will walk you out.
MOD_VOY_HELP_FUEL_WHY: Fuel is for the campfire, so the sea costs food only.
MOD_VOY_HELP_ROOM_LEVEL: At Voyage level ${level}. Every level adds ${food} HP of food and ${fuel} fuel.
MOD_VOY_HELP_LOAD_WHERE: Load food and fuel from your bank standing on a place or next to it. The table shows how much of it reaches the stores.
MOD_VOY_HELP_NIGHT_LIGHT: The fuel a trip leaves over lights the way:
MOD_VOY_HELP_NIGHT_XP: A lit hex gives ${bonus}% more Voyage XP.
MOD_VOY_HELP_WORN: Below ${worn}% it keeps out of deep water.
MOD_VOY_HELP_WORN_THROUGH: Worn through, it only heads for the coast.
MOD_VOY_HELP_PITCH: Pitch comes from Firemaking: ${chance}% a log at level 1, more with better logs.
MOD_VOY_HELP_HOLD_SLOTS: The hold keeps bank items aboard, bank-style: one kind of item a slot, in any amount.
MOD_VOY_HELP_HOLD_WHERE: Stand on your ship or next to it.
MOD_VOY_HELP_HOLD_SELL: To sell items, take them out at the ship and sell them at a market.
MOD_VOY_HELP_HOLD_SAVE: The hold is in the mod's save data. Take everything out before removing the mod, or it is lost.
MOD_VOY_HELP_XP_FAST_TRAVEL: A fast-travel hop by ship counts its hexes as water.
MOD_VOY_HELP_NO_XP_REACH: Moves back toward land from beyond your ship's reach.
MOD_VOY_HELP_COMPASS_BANK: It works while it is in your bank.
MOD_VOY_HELP_COMPASS_POINTS: When a skill doesn't work where you stand (Mining, Woodcutting, Smithing and the like), the compass points toward the nearest place where it does.
MOD_VOY_HELP_COMPASS_PANEL: On the map, when you tap or click a locked skill in the "You are here" panel.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_HULL_COST: Every ${step}% takes ${logs} logs (the cheapest first) and ${pitch} Pitch.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_LAND: Skills work only where the land allows: trees for Woodcutting, water for Fishing, a town for crafting.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_SURVEY: Survey with Cartography to see what is around you.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_TRADE_WHERE: You can sell and buy only in or next to a town, port or market.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_COMBAT: Your skills start locked, so your first coins come from combat.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_COMBAT_LINE: The Combat line on the map lists the areas you can fight in from where you stand.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_PURSE: You have ${gp} GP for the road.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_COMPASS: It is in your bank and points to the nearest place where a locked skill works.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_SHARPEN: Levelling Voyage sharpens it; the shop sells a spare.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_RULE_WATER: You need a ship to go on the water.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_RULE_BOARD: Board it by stepping onto its hex.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_RULE_ASHORE: When you step ashore, it waits where you left it.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_FAR_REACH: A dinghy keeps within ${reach} hexes of a coast it can land on.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_FAR_BACK: You are farther out, so for now it can only head back toward one.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_NEW_PAGE: A new page in your journal: ${title}
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_FOOTER: Read about it in the journal: ${title}
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_FOOTER_NEW: A new page in your journal: ${title}
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CRAFTS_ANYWHERE: Anywhere at all: ${skills}. Each constellation still shows only from its own sky.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CRAFTS_RELAXED: Relaxed rules are on: making things works anywhere, and only gathering keeps to its ground.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_INTRO: If you are reading this, the Old Man has gone ashore for good, and the book is yours now.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_WHO_BODY:
I was a ship's master once, on the long run to the far shores. My crews called me the Old Man, as crews do, and the name stayed when the ships were gone.
When my knees gave out I took a room above a chandler's and wrote down what the roads and the sea had taught me.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_BOOK_BODY:
The first pages are the rules of the road, as I learnt them. The rest I left blank for you: what you find, where you find it, and the places you pass ([[tab:resources|Resources]], [[tab:places|Places]]).
The compass came with it. It knew the way better than I did, and it never told me more than I had earned.
The ${journal} key opens this book from any page, and closes it again; so does the book button at the top, by the potions.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_BOOK_BODY_OF:
The first pages are the rules of the road, as I learnt them. The rest I left blank for you: what you find, where you find it, and the places you pass ([[tab:resources|Resources]], [[tab:places|Places]]).
The compass came with it. It knew the way better than I did, and it never told me more than I had earned.
The book button at the top, by the potions, opens this book from any page. A keyboard key can do the same: set one in Mod Settings, section Voyage.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_YOU_BODY:
A book like this is no use in a drawer. It wants feet under it.
Write in it. Cross out what I got wrong. And when you reach a shore I never saw, put it down plainly, so the next one need not learn it twice.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: the Old Man's pages are the rules of this mod in his words. Where he and the Voyage page disagree, the page is right and he is out of date.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CRAFTS_TITLE: Where each craft can be done
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CRAFTS_INTRO: I write this down so I need not learn it twice. The land decides what a hand can do: an axe wants trees, a net wants water, a forge wants a town.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CRAFTS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: every town lets you do every craft, so there is always a place to go back to.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_STORES_INTRO: Every hex walked or sailed costs bread, and rough or cold ground costs fire as well. Not every place will load a full measure.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_STORES_NOTE: Why the measure differs: a port loads straight from quay and chandler; in a town you haul it through the streets and pay the middlemen; a market sells food, and firewood is a hauler's trade; a farm spares what it can.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SHIP_INTRO: A hull wears with every hex of sea, more in deep water. I keep her tight with timber and Pitch, as sailors always have.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SHIP_NOTE: Why a ship burns no wood: fire was a crew's worst fear. The galley stove sat on a bed of sand, lit at set hours under watch. What a ship truly wore out at sea was its food and its own hull.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_HOLD_INTRO: What I would rather not carry, the boat can: a few slots of anything, reached only where the boat is.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_HOLD_NOTE: The hold belongs to the boat, not to me. If I leave her on a far beach, what is in her waits there too.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRAVELS_INTRO: Every hex I cross teaches me something of the road. Water teaches more than land, and a hex crossed by lamplight more still.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRAVELS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: walking on an empty belly or drifting home pays nothing, so the road can't be farmed.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_COMPASS_INTRO: It does not show the way; it tells me how warm I am. The better I know the sea, the more it says.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_COMPASS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: the compass only speaks when the map has nothing to say. A place you know is always the better guide.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_INTRO: A chart is only as good as the eye that reads it. Here is how I read mine.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: every hex was coloured by hand from the game's own art, so the tint and the picture should agree. If they don't, tell me.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_TINT_BODY:
A surveyed hex is tinted by its land: green grasslands, white snow, red badlands, and so on. The Legend in the panel names them all, and [[ch:lands|The lands and what stands on them]] says what each allows.
A hex not yet surveyed shows nothing new. Survey with Cartography to see what it is.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_PANEL_BODY:
The panel at the top left of the map tells me the land under my feet, its features and the place, if there is one.
Trade and Combat say whether I can sell or fight here, and name the area.
Works here lists the skills this hex allows. Tap one to see what is found here: which trees, rocks or fish.
Locked here lists the rest. Tap one to see what it needs and the nearest place I know where it works.
Manage voyage opens the Voyage page; the book button opens this journal.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_KEYS_BODY:
On the map, the ${key} key brings me back to where I stand, like the map's own home button.
The key can be changed or cleared in Mod Settings, section Voyage.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_KEYS_BODY_OFF:
The map's home button brings me back to where I stand.
A keyboard key can do the same: set one in Mod Settings, section Voyage.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_MARKS_BODY:
Show on map, under [[tab:resources|Resources]] and [[tab:places|Places]], draws a gold border round every hex I wrote down and turns the map to the nearest.
The marks go when I move on or open the journal again.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LANDS_TITLE: The lands and what stands on them
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LANDS_INTRO: Every hex is one kind of land, and the land decides what a hand can do there. What stands on it, a river, a forest, a town, can add more.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LANDS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: these are the rules, not the riches. Where each ore, tree and fish lies is for you to find, and it goes into [[tab:resources|Resources]] as you do.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LANDS_KINDS_BODY:
Once surveyed, a hex is tinted with the colour of its land, as in the map's Legend.
What a hex costs to cross is in [[ch:stores|Victuals and fuel]].
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LANDS_FEATURES_BODY:
The panel names a hex's features after its land: "Grasslands · Cliff, Holy". These are the ones a craft looks for.
Most workshop crafts also work one hex out from their place: see [[guide:grace|Grace: one hex out]].
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_LANDS_DRY: ${skills} work on any dry land, so they are left out.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_TITLE: A few tricks of the road
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_INTRO: Nobody told me these. I learnt them the slow way, so you need not.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: none of these are needed. They only save you a walk or two.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_STORES_BODY:
Load at a port when you can: it gives the full measure, a town or market a little less, a farm, village or camp half ([[ch:stores|the table]]).
Every Voyage level makes room for more food and fuel.
With empty stores you can still walk easy ground. It earns no Voyage XP, but it gets you home.
Snow and lava eat fuel fastest. Load up before you cross them.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_BOAT_BODY:
Put by 500 GP and 50 Normal Logs early: the dinghy is built on any coast.
The boat waits where you step ashore. Leave her where you will come back.
Fast travel between ports sails your boat, so she has to be at the port you leave from.
Beach her to mend the hull: logs and Pitch, which Firemaking gives now and then ([[ch:ship|The boat and her hull]]). Keep a little Pitch in the bank.
Below half her hull she keeps out of deep water, so mend her before a long crossing.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_NIGHT_BODY:
Travel after dark when you can: the fuel left over from a trip lights the way, and a lit hex gives 25% more Voyage XP ([[ch:travels|Miles behind me]]).
Light never takes the fuel a trip needs, so night is never worse than day.
Firemaking levels make the fuel go further; Astrology levels make the light go further.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_WAY_BODY:
Survey before you wander: the compass and the panel name only places you have surveyed.
Many crafts work one hex out from their place. Stand next to the town if the town itself is busy with something else.
What you find is written under [[tab:resources|Resources]]. Search it by the item you want, not only by the rock or tree.
Voyage level 10 makes the compass count the hexes; level 25 makes it name the place ([[ch:compass|The Wayfinder's Compass]]).
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_TITLE: If the road is too hard
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_INTRO: Not every traveller wants every hardship. The rules can be softened, one by one.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: play the way you enjoy. Turning a rule off is not cheating; it is choosing your road.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_EASIER_BODY:
All of these are in Mod Settings, section Voyage.
Relaxed keeps gathering tied to the land and lets every craft work anywhere.
Resource zones off lets every tree, rock and fish of a skill grow wherever the skill works.
Combat, trade and provisions can each be switched off on their own.
Night can be moved to suit your hours, or switched off.
Voyage rules off lifts every lock at once; the map colours and the panel stay.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_WHY_BODY:
The world map is beautiful, and the base game lets you ignore it. These rules make it matter: where you stand decides what you can do.
Each rule follows the real world as far as a game allows: trees in forests, fish in water, forges in towns, food from farms.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LEAVING_INTRO: Every voyage ends somewhere. If this one ends here, end it with care.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LEAVING_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: the game keeps a mod's data only while the mod is loaded. That is the game's rule, not mine, and I cannot work around it.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LEAVING_WHAT_BODY:
Load your character without the mod and save, and everything of Voyage is gone for good: Voyage XP, the boat, her hold and all in it, your stores and this journal.
The mod's own items in your bank go too: the compass and any Pitch.
Putting the mod back later starts it all from the beginning.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LEAVING_HOW_BODY:
Take everything out of the hold on the Voyage page first ([[ch:hold|The hold]]): those are your own items, and they come back to the bank.
Sell the compass and the Pitch if you want their coins.
Everything else of the base game stays as it is.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_ADVENTURE_INTRO: In this country every skill must be bought, and I had nothing to sell. The first coins came from the sword.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_ADVENTURE_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: the fight on this page is worked out afresh from where you stand, each time you open it.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_ADVENTURE_FIRST_BODY: Fighting needs you on the area's hex or next to it. Walk there before you pick a monster.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_ADVENTURE_NEXT_BODY:
Buy a skill whose land is around you: the panel's Locked here tells what each skill needs and where, and [[ch:lands|The lands and what stands on them]] lists it all.
Keep enough GP for the road to a trading place, where the loot can be sold. [[tab:places|Places]] lists the ones you know.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LIGHTHOUSE_INTRO: Every coast I ever left had a light on it, and so did every coast I came home to.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LIGHTHOUSE_LAST_BODY:
This is the last page I wrote. The ones after it are yours.
I kept the lighthouse for the end because it is what I looked for at the end of every voyage: one steady light, and a keeper who never asks where you have been.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LIGHTHOUSE_LIGHT_BODY:
There are lights on this coast still. Find them for yourself; that is half the pleasure.
When the road is long and the stores run low, turn for home before you must. A captain who comes back can always sail again.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LIGHTHOUSE_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: thank you for sailing with this mod. The land is still being written, and there are more shores to come.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_LIGHTHOUSE_ALT: An ink drawing of a lighthouse on a rock, its light sweeping over the sea, with a small sail on the horizon.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_HIRE_INTRO: No master sails alone. Ashore they call them Folks; aboard I called them my crew, and I paid them on the nail.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_HIRE_START_BODY:
Buy the Trainee Licence in the shop, under Worker Folks. It brings your first Shift Slot.
Then hire a Trainee. Every hand of a rank you already keep makes the next one of that rank a fifth dearer.
The Hiring page in the sidebar is your muster board: who works, at what, and who is owed.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_HIRE_WORKER_BODY:
Every skill page has a Worker box. Pick a Folk there instead of You, then start the work as you always would.
A Folk holds one skill while you do another, and keeps at it while you are away.
To take a skill back, switch the box to You. The Folk stops when you start work on that page.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_HIRE_PORT_BODY:
On this map, signing, promoting and dismissing a hand need a town, the capital or a port, as Township does ([[ch:crafts|Where each craft can be done]]).
Putting a hand to work does not. Sign them in port, then send them to work from anywhere.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_HIRE_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: these pages show because Worker Folks: Hiring is loaded. They hold its numbers as of its version 1.1.0; its own pages in the game have the last word.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_RANKS_INTRO: A good hand is made, not hired. Each rank works faster and wastes less, and costs more.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_RANKS_TIERS_BODY:
Under 100, the produce rate is the chance that a try comes good. Over 100, the rest is the chance of a second batch.
Wages are by the hour of work, paid per action, failed ones too.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_RANKS_LICENCES_B:
Each rank needs its licence first: a Hiring level, coins, a dungeon cleared, and a few items besides.
Your best licence also caps the Shift Slots: 2, 4, 7, 10, then as many as you like.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_RANKS_PROMOTE_BO: A hand is promoted, not hired again. It takes the next licence, the hand's own mastery at 20, 40, 60 or 80, a diploma item, and 60% of that rank's next hire price.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_RANKS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: the wages here are Standard difficulty. The Worker Folks difficulty setting scales them.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_INTRO: Pay your crew before you pay yourself. I learnt that one the hard way, halfway to nowhere.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_WAGES_BODY:
Wages come from the Payroll Reserve first, then from the bank. The reserve opens at Hiring 5 and holds more as the level grows.
A fresh hand earns 40% of the rank's wage. It rises to the full wage at that hand's mastery 99: seniority costs money.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_GRACE_BODY: An unpaid hand keeps working for 15 minutes of work, 30 from that hand's mastery 25. Put coins back in time and the debt is paid on the next action.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_STRIKE_BODY:
After the grace the hand strikes: the skill stops and the slot comes free.
Settling costs the owed wages and a severance, then a rest: 30 minutes for a Trainee, up to 8 hours for a Foreman. An apology costs three times the severance and skips the rest.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_EASIER_HEAD: If the wages are too steep
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_EASIER_BODY:
Mod Settings, Worker Folks, Wage difficulty: from No sweat (free, no strikes) to Evil hardcore (five times the wage). Standard is the default.
No sweat only puts an old strike or debt on hold. It comes back on a paid difficulty.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: a hand who dies on the job freezes the slot for a day of real time. A thieving hand eats your combat food below 60% health, so keep some selected.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_TIPS_INTRO: Things I would tell a new master on the quay, if they would listen.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_TIPS_OWN_BODY:
Do your signing, promoting and dismissing while you are in port. Out on the road the Hiring page can only watch.
Fill the Payroll Reserve before a long voyage: wages run while you are away, and they do not wait for the tide.
Hands wear their own gear, never yours: the Gear button on each card.
A Foreman lifts every other working hand's XP by 3%, up to 15%.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_TIPS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: the tips under From the crew's own book come straight from Worker Folks, so they stay as its author keeps them.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_RESOURCES_TITLE: What I have found, and where
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_RESOURCES_EMPTY: Nothing yet. The first time I gather something somewhere, it is written here.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_SEARCH_NONE: Nothing about “${query}” in the journal yet.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_NOT_FOUND_YET: Not found yet, only ruled out.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_HEAT_CANVAS: Map. Arrow keys move it, plus and minus zoom, 0 shows the whole map.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_HEAT_HELP: Drag to move, scroll or pinch to zoom. Point at a hex to read it.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CHART_DROP: ${name}: a chart of one country. Use it in your journal, under Resources.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CHART_FREE: Voyage ${level}: a free chart. Use it in your journal, under Resources.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_PICK_INTRO: A chart marks the whole country of one find: every hex where it works. The heat map shows it, and the compass and the hints may use it. A chart is never undone.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_PICK_NONE: Nothing left to chart for this craft at your level.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CHARTED_LINE: Charted: ${count} hexes where it works. The heat map shows them in pale gold.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_PLACES_EMPTY: No places yet. Fights, trades and discoveries are written here.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_PLACES_SEARCH_LABEL: Search by place, land or monster
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GOLBIN_NOTE: Golbin. They spell it so in this country, and I gave up arguing.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GOLBIN_ALT: A pencil sketch of a golbin in a crooked crown, scratching his head, a small dagger in his other hand. Beside him the word GOBLIN is written at a slant, the BL struck out and LB written above it.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_INTRO: A page is written the first time a rule stops me. The blank ones wait for their day.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_NONE: No lesson yet. The first rule that stops me will be written here.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_TERRAIN_BODY:
Today I took my tools to the wrong ground and got nothing for it. A craft works only where the land has what it needs.
The lock names the nearest place I know where it works. If I know none, it says so, and then I must survey or ask the compass.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_TERRAIN_POINTS:
Gathering wants the right ground: trees, rock, water, soil.
Making things wants a workshop: a town, a camp, a forge, a temple.
Poorer ground is slower, but the work still goes.
The whole table is in [[ch:crafts|Where each craft can be done]], and land by land in [[ch:lands|The lands and what stands on them]].
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ZONE_TITLE: Each thing has its own country
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ZONE_BODY:
The ground was right, but what I wanted was not there. Each ore, tree, fish, crop and mark has its own country, as in the real world: copper in dry red land, tin washed down rivers, mithril in the frozen north.
Every place I found something is written under Resources, and every place I came up empty, so I need not try twice.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ZONE_POINTS:
Search [[tab:resources|Resources]] by the thing you want, or by what it gives.
Show on map marks every hex where I found it.
The stars are the same: each constellation shows only from its own band of sky, away from town lights.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_GRACE_BODY: I worked a craft one hex away from its proper place, at full speed. Some crafts reach a little past their town, mine or temple, the way a smith works in the yard outside the forge as well as in it.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_GRACE_POINTS:
Mining, Thieving, Smithing, Crafting, Herblore, Runecrafting, Alt. Magic, Summoning and Township reach one hex out.
Grace never reaches onto the water or under cloud.
The hex one out shares its neighbour's resources: a thief next to a town finds the town's marks.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_TRADE_BODY: Coins are no use where there is nobody to take them. I can sell and buy only in or next to a town, port or market.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_TRADE_POINTS:
The panel on the map says whether trade works where I stand.
Places I have traded at are written under [[tab:places|Places]].
If I am ever stranded with nothing to pay my way, a wandering trader finds me.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_COMBAT_BODY: A fight happens where the enemy lives. I must stand on a combat area's own hex, or one next to it, to fight there. Dungeons and strongholds are the same.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_COMBAT_POINTS:
The panel's Combat line lists the fights I can start from where I stand.
Areas I have fought in are written under [[tab:places|Places]], with Show on map.
Walking away stops the fight.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_COMPASS_BODY: I found a compass in my pack the day I arrived. It points to the nearest place where a locked craft works, and says how warm I am: Hot, Warm, Cold or Freezing.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_COMPASS_POINTS:
It speaks only when I know no such place myself.
Levelling Voyage teaches it to count the hexes, then to name the place ([[ch:compass|The Wayfinder's Compass]]).
If I lose it, the shop sells another.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_STRANDED_BODY: I came to a place with nothing left to pay my way. A wandering trader found me, as one always will: nobody is left stuck for good.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_STRANDED_POINTS:
He buys at half price where there is no market.
When my stores can't carry me to safe ground, he walks me there.
Any honest way to earn coin, a fight, a pocket picked, a town's taxes, means I am not stranded.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_DINGHY_BODY: Nobody stands on open water without a boat. I build my first dinghy on the Voyage page, standing on a coast, from coin and logs.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_DINGHY_POINTS:
To board, I step onto the boat's hex; to land, I step onto a coast.
The boat waits where I leave her, so I had better remember where that was.
A dinghy keeps close to land; bigger hulls go farther ([[ch:ship|The boat and her hull]]).
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ISLAND_BODY: I could see the island, but my hull could not land on it. Each island wants a hull of its own size, in the order its dungeons are meant to be met.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ISLAND_POINTS:
Western Isle, Golden Isle and Frost Island take a dinghy.
The Cursed Isle needs a longboat, the Ominous Isle a brig.
I may always walk on and leave an island I am already on.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_FOUND_BOTH: You found a compass and a journal. I wonder what's inside.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_JOURNAL: It fills as you go: what you find and where, the places you have been, and a page for each rule the first time it stops you.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_JOURNAL_WHERE: Open it with the book button at the bottom right of any skill page, or beside Manage voyage on the map.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_EMPTY: No voyage planned. Choose Plan voyage on a page of the Captain's Journal, or in a popup that sends you elsewhere.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_VERDICT_CLEAR: The way is clear. Travel there yourself, or sail it in one go with Navigator's Charts.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_VERDICT_COSTS: You can't pay the travel costs yet.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_VERDICT_SHORT: Not enough food or fuel, and nowhere on the way to load more. Load at a port, town, market or farm first.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_VERDICT_ASHORE: Not enough food left to get back ashore from there.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_VERDICT_HULL: The hull is too worn for this route. Repair it first.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_VERDICT_NOWAY: No charted way there that your vessel can take.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_VERDICT_UNCHARTED: You haven't charted the way there yet: survey it first.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_STOPPED: The voyage stopped at ${at}. Plan it again from here.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_START_FAILED: Arrived, but ${name} could not be started.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_NAV_NEED: Sail! takes you the whole way in one click. It needs Navigator's Charts: from Voyage level ${level}, bought at a port, once.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_NAV_WHY_PORT: Sold at ports: stand on one to buy them.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_NAV_WHY_COST: Not enough GP or Pitch yet.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_NAV_BOUGHT: Navigator's Charts bought: Plan a voyage can now sail you there.
